name: Scout
job: Finds places worth adding to your map, checks them, and explains why each one fits your taste.

steps.d: Reads the pin you opened, or the pins in view, and searches your other pins for related threads like a band, film or architect. Your pin descriptions are how it learns your taste.
Searches for candidate places and reads the pages it finds: up to 8 searches for Pin Scout, 12 for Area Scout. Every claim it later makes has to point back to one of these pages.
Code geocodes each candidate, measures the distance, and checks for duplicates and past decisions. Anything that fails is moved to Rejected with the rule it broke. Scout gets one chance to resubmit.
The model decides what genuinely fits your taste and what's worth the detour. It must cite the pins that make the case, and its sources.

Results slide up from the bottom: photos, why each was chosen, and sources. Accept opens your normal add form. Reject works in one press, with an optional reason. Every decision is remembered, and the last run survives a refresh.

locked.d: Come from geocoding in this run, never the model's guess.
Pin Scout: within 60 km of the pin.
Area Scout: inside the area on your screen.
Not within 500 m of a pin, and not the same name (case, accents, apostrophes and "the" ignored).
Never re-suggests what you accepted or rejected.
Every suggestion links to a page found in this run's own searches.
Up to 3 for a pin, 10 for an area. Extras are cut.
An empty result needs a reason, not filler.

judged.d: Argued from your own pins, which it has to name.
Telling a real find from a tourist trap.
The summary and the "why Scout chose it" text in your tray. Names come out in Title Case, never with an ampersand.
Coming with Connections: a specific named thread ("Stanley Kubrick", not "70s feel") with two sources.

story.intro: A user story extended for agents. The first line is the concept. The lines after it force the technical decisions into the open, so they're made on purpose instead of downstream.
story.when: I press Scout on a pin or on the area I'm looking at
story.so_that: I can plan trips around what I care about

rows.label: It may
rows.text: search the web, read my pins, look up coordinates, measure distances, and check for duplicates and past decisions.

rows.label: It must never
rows.text: add a pin, guess a location, or re-suggest something I've already accepted or rejected.

rows.label: It decides
rows.text: what fits my taste and what's worth showing.

rows.label: It stops when
rows.text: it has up to 3 strong finds near a pin (10 for an area), or none are good enough; or at its limits of 8 searches (12 for an area) and 20 steps; or when I press Stop.

rows.label: I'll know it works when
rows.text: I accept at least a third of what it shows.

howto: Write the first line before anything else. If you can't, the agent isn't defined yet.
Ask whether it needs to be an agent at all. If the steps are always the same, a fixed pipeline is simpler and more reliable. (Adding a pin is a pipeline, not an agent, for exactly this reason.)
"It must never" and "It decides" are the boundary between code and model. Every "never" should be enforced in code, not only stated in the prompt.
Update the story whenever the agent changes, and add a line to the changelog.
